panels.title: How to read this dashboard during a load test
panels.description: Reading order for the live demo.

options.content:
**Read top to bottom:**

1. **Traffic & SLO** - redirect p99 under 50 ms, 5xx under 0.1 %, RPS tracking the k6 arrival rate (RPS flat while k6 drops iterations = saturated).
2. **Cache** - hit ratio should climb to ~100 % as the seeded links warm up; misses go to Postgres.
3. **Database** - Npgsql *requests waiting for a connection* > 0 means the pool is exhausted (usually the first bottleneck); compare Postgres backends with max_connections.
4. **Click pipeline** - enqueued = published = processed; a growing queue/buffer or dropped clicks means analytics is falling behind (redirects are unaffected by design).
5. **Saturation** - thread-pool queue, GC pauses and CPU per api instance show which resource ran out first.

Dots on latency graphs are trace exemplars (click to open the trace in Tempo). k6, logs and slow traces are at the bottom.

panels.title: Total requests/s
panels.description: All api requests per second (health checks excluded); should track the k6 arrival rate.

panels.title: Redirect p99 (target < 50 ms)
panels.description: 99th percentile latency of GET /{code}; red means the latency SLO is breached.

panels.title: Redirects under 50 ms
panels.description: Share of redirects answered within 50 ms (the SLI behind the p99 target).

panels.title: 5xx error ratio (target < 0.1 %)
panels.description: Share of requests answered with 5xx; red means the error SLO is breached.

panels.title: API replicas
panels.description: Live api instances (distinct service_instance_id still reporting CPU time); shows scaling.

panels.title: Worker replicas
panels.description: Live analytics worker instances (distinct service_instance_id still reporting).

panels.title: Requests/s by route
panels.description: Redirect and REST API traffic per route and method; the redirect route should dominate.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99: redirect vs API
panels.description: Server-side latency from the ASP.NET Core histogram; dashed line = 50 ms redirect target. Dots are trace exemplars.

panels.title: API p99 latency by route
panels.description: p99 per REST route; shows which API call (e.g. create = a write) is slow.

panels.title: 5xx error ratio
panels.description: Share of requests failing with 5xx; dashed line = 0.1 % error budget.

panels.title: 4xx responses/s by status
panels.description: Client errors stacked by status: 404 unknown code, 410 expired/deleted, 401 bad key, 429 rate-limited.

panels.title: Requests/s per api instance
panels.description: Load per replica; nginx should spread traffic evenly, and new replicas should pick up load.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: (hit + negative_hit) / all lookups; low = most redirects go to Postgres.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio over time
panels.description: Should rise as the cache warms up; a drop puts load on the database.

panels.title: Cache lookups/s by result
panels.description: Redis lookups for redirects: hit, miss (goes to Postgres), negative_hit (cached 404/410).

panels.title: Cache lookup latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Time of one Redis GET from the api; rising values mean Redis or the network is saturated.

panels.title: Redis commands/s and clients
panels.description: Server-side Redis throughput (left) and connected clients (right axis) from redis_exporter.

panels.title: Redis memory, evictions, keyspace hits/misses
panels.description: Used memory vs maxmemory (left); evicted keys/s and keyspace hits/misses per second (right).

panels.title: Requests waiting for a DB connection
panels.description: Npgsql pending connection requests across selected api instances; > 0 means the pool is exhausted.

panels.title: Npgsql pool: in use vs idle vs max (api)
panels.description: Connections in the api pools (selected instances), stacked by state; dashed red = pool maximum.

panels.title: Requests waiting for a connection, per instance
panels.description: Npgsql pending requests per api instance (and worker); the likely first bottleneck under load.

panels.title: Npgsql command duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Client-side time per database command (api and worker), including network and lock waits.

panels.title: Npgsql commands/s, failures and pool timeouts
panels.description: Database command rate per service (left); failed commands and connection-pool timeouts per second (right).

panels.title: Postgres connections vs max_connections
panels.description: Server-side backends by state (postgres-exporter); dashed red = max_connections. N api replicas x pool size can exceed it.

panels.title: Postgres transactions/s and rows/s
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks (left) and rows fetched/inserted/updated per second (right) in the shortener database.

panels.title: Active backends by wait event
panels.description: What active Postgres backends wait on; 'Lock' rising = row contention (e.g. sync click UPDATEs on hot links).

panels.title: Locks and deadlocks
panels.description: Held locks by mode (left) and deadlocks per second (right) in the shortener database.

panels.title: Click flow: enqueued -> published -> processed
panels.description: Clicks per second at each stage; the three lines should overlap. A gap means a stage is falling behind.

panels.title: Clicks lost or failed
panels.description: Dropped (buffer full), publish failures, worker batch failures and dead-lettered messages per second; should be zero.

panels.title: In-memory click buffer per api instance
panels.description: Clicks waiting in each api's bounded buffer; dashed red = capacity 10 000, where clicks start being dropped.

panels.title: RabbitMQ queue depth
panels.description: Ready + unacknowledged messages in clicks.analytics and the DLQ; a growing backlog means workers can't keep up.

panels.title: RabbitMQ publish vs deliver vs ack
panels.description: Broker-wide messages received from publishers, delivered to consumers and acknowledged per second.

panels.title: Click lag p50 / p95 / p99 (redirect -> stored)
panels.description: Time from the redirect to the click being written to Postgres; the end-to-end freshness of stats.

panels.title: Worker clicks processed/s per instance
panels.description: Throughput of each worker replica; shows whether adding workers adds throughput.

panels.title: Worker batch size
panels.description: Average and p95 clicks per batch write; batches near the max (500) mean the worker is running flat out.

panels.title: Worker batch duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Time to write one batch to Postgres; rising values point at database contention.

panels.title: Process CPU per instance (cores)
panels.description: CPU time used per second by each api process (1 = one full core); compare with the container's CPU limit.

panels.title: Thread pool queue length
panels.description: Work items waiting for a thread-pool thread; sustained growth = thread-pool starvation (sync-over-async or CPU-bound).

panels.title: Thread pool threads
panels.description: Thread-pool threads per instance; a steady climb means the pool is injecting threads to cope with blocking.

panels.title: GC collections/s by generation
panels.description: Garbage collections per second; frequent gen2 collections hurt tail latency.

panels.title: Time paused in GC
panels.description: Fraction of wall time each process is paused for garbage collection.

panels.title: Process working set
panels.description: Physical memory used by each api process.

panels.title: Kestrel connections
panels.description: Active and queued connections per instance; queued > 0 means Kestrel can't accept connections fast enough.

panels.title: In-flight requests per instance
panels.description: Concurrent HTTP requests being processed; rises sharply when a dependency slows down.

panels.title: Rate-limit rejections/s
panels.description: Requests rejected with 429 by the Redis-backed limiter, by bucket and caller type.

panels.title: k6 request rate by status
panels.description: Requests per second sent by k6, by HTTP status; compare with server-side RPS.

panels.title: k6 virtual users
panels.description: Active and allocated VUs; with an arrival-rate executor VUs rise when responses slow down.

panels.title: k6 dropped iterations/s
panels.description: Iterations k6 could not start on schedule: the target arrival rate was NOT achieved (not enough VUs / system too slow).

panels.title: k6 failed requests and checks
panels.description: Failed requests per second (left) and check pass rate since test start (right).

panels.title: k6 http_req_duration p50 / p95 / p99 / max (client side, cumulative since test start)
panels.description: Client-observed latency per scenario from k6 remote write; k6 computes these over the whole run, so they move slowly.

panels.title: Warnings and errors per minute
panels.description: Log records at Warning or above, by service and level (Loki, from OTLP logs).

panels.title: Warning and error logs
panels.description: Most recent Warning+ logs from api and worker; expand a line for trace_id to jump to the trace.

panels.title: Slow (> 100 ms) or failed api traces
panels.description: Recent api traces with a span over 100 ms or an error; click a trace ID to open it.

panels.title: Failed worker traces
panels.description: Recent worker traces with an error span (failed batch writes, dead-lettering).
